notes:
Summary: Quantum Helpline builds AI-first contact center tooling for mid-market telco and fintech support orgs. We're in an evaluation POC for agent-assist + ticket summarization. Key ask: robust RAG over multi-source KBs with verifiable citations and freshness controls; system must survive large evening spikes during billing cycles.

Customer quotes / paraphrases: "We need the AI to cite where an answer came from — agent must be able to paste or open source doc quickly. Freshness is non-negotiable — nightly syncs not enough for outage KB."

Requirements (from tech + product):
- Data sources: Zendesk historic tickets (~4M), Confluence knowledge base, S3-hosted transcripts and policy PDFs.
- Retrieval: multi-source retrieval with source attribution per snippet; must present top-3 citations with link and confidence score.
- Freshness: near-real-time ingestion for high-priority docs (<=1 hour latency), 24h TTL for certain dynamic KBs, incremental updates for policy pages.
- Models & routing: prefer open/hostable models for Dedicated/Private deployment; require automatic fallback to a smaller, cheaper model for sustained bursts.
- Latency / throughput targets: baseline 200 qps sustained for search-only queries; burst to 1000 qps for 1–5 minutes during billing spikes; P95 end-to-end suggestion latency target <= 300ms for short queries, <= 800ms for long RAG flows (including retrieval).
- Cost sensitivity: unit-cost control via batching and caching; want Redwood Optimize suggestions for quantization and batching thresholds.
- Reliability & fallbacks: automatic model routing by policy (latency-first for live chat, cost-first for batch summaries); transparent fallbacks with indicator to agent.
- Security/compliance: SOC2 required, SSO/SAML + SCIM, encryption-at-rest w/ KMS, audit logs for each generated response, support for EU data residency.

POC plan (what we'll run):
1) Week 1: Ingest a 250k-document slice (Zendesk + Confluence + 30 days of transcripts). Validate connector reliability and doc freshness.
2) Week 2: Evaluate retrieval latency & relevance across Pinecone + Milvus + local IVF index; measure P50/P95 retrieval times and citation accuracy.
3) Week 3: End-to-end latency tests with hosted and dedicated model variants; run spike simulation (1k qps for 3 minutes) and observe autoscaling/fallback behavior.
4) Week 4: Agent UX test — tool-calling actions (create ticket, escalate, add tag) and summarization quality review with human raters.

Open questions from customer:
- Does Redwood provide an out-of-the-box citation format tied to source doc anchors? (asked 2026-02-26)
- Can we set different freshness policies per source and per doc-type?
- Will Dedicated support hot-warm index tiers to optimize cost for infrequently accessed KBs?

Stitched negotiation notes:
- Customer prefers Private deployment for regulated telco customers but would consider Dedicated if guarantees on region residency + KMS provided.
- Price sensitivity around burst pricing; they asked for predictable tiered cap with overage protection.

Next step: finish ingestion tests (scheduled 2026-03-07), Redwood SE to produce a short delivery plan for data residency + citation UX, legal to receive SOC2 artifacts (drive link).
